relevance.rationale: Genuine orphan, and after a careful read of the abstract, index terms and introduction the honest verdict is no bearing. It establishes existence and uniqueness conditions for quaternion reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces via left quaternion Hilbert spaces, gives quaternion Riesz-representation and Moore-Aronszajn theorems, and validates the resulting kernels in ridge-regression applications on inertial body-sensor data and nonlinear channel equalisation. This is statistical signal processing / kernel learning. The word 'quaternion' does appear in 16 folio content files, which is exactly the kind of lexical coincidence that inflates a triage: those hits are the SU(2)-to-SO(3) double cover (rem:quaternion-so3-motivation, su2-so3-intro) and quaternionic spectral resolvents on the folio's surface — quaternions as a geometric structure, not as a scalar field over which one builds an RKHS for regression. There is no kernel method, no learning problem and no regression anywhere in the folio. Recording this as not-relevant rather than tangential because the field itself does not overlap; the shared word does.

proposedActions.rationale: Read and judged to need nothing: the folio contains no kernel-method, RKHS or regression content, and its quaternion usage is the SU(2)/SO(3) geometric one.
